title: Book 3 — Thalia, Chapter 420
paragraphs: Then when the Ichthyophagoi asked the king in return about the length of days and the manner of life of his people, he answered that the majority of them reached the age of a hundred and twenty years, and some went beyond even this; their food was boiled flesh and their drink was milk. When the spies marveled at the number of years, he led them to a certain spring, in the water of which they washed and came out with their skin more sleek, as if it were a spring of oil; and from it came a scent as of violets. The water of this spring, the spies said, was so extraordinarily weak that nothing could float upon it, not wood nor anything lighter than wood — everything sank to the bottom. If this water they have is really such as it is said to be, it would no doubt be the cause why the people are so long-lived, since they use it for every purpose of life. Then when they left this spring, he led them to a prison for men, where all were bound in fetters of gold. Among these Ethiopians bronze is the rarest and most precious of all things. When they had seen the prison, they also saw the so-called Table of the Sun:
